question: Should a configured Discord role mention deliberately wake every eligible bot that has that role, and what guild/channel opt-in and anti-fan-out policy should govern that behavior?
rationale: The request introduces a new activation and configuration contract whose fan-out behavior cannot be inferred safely from existing direct-mention or sender-allowlist semantics.

options.title: Adopt explicit opt-in role triggers
options.body: Add a separately named guild/channel role-ID trigger list and define deterministic fan-out, precedence, and loop-protection behavior.

options.title: Defer to broader access-policy design
options.body: Fold role-trigger activation into the broader Discord access-policy redesign only if maintainers want one unified authorization and mention model.

options.title: Keep direct mentions only
options.body: Reject shared-role activation to preserve one-bot targeting and avoid coordinated-response fan-out.

recommendation.title: Adopt explicit opt-in role triggers
recommendation.body: Add a separately named guild/channel role-ID trigger list and define deterministic fan-out, precedence, and loop-protection behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review already identified this as a maintainer product decision on the Discord mention-gating boundary.
